item.title: DOLLHOUSE: TRANS DAY OF REMEMBERANCE BENEFIT — Sat Nov 21, 8:00 PM — 2A Osler St
item.description: /lineup MISSMADAME FKA MS.MYLES V1NOV1NA FKA Sofia Fly Syana Delicious DJ NO*MAD Doll House is an event series put on by DJs and Community Organizers Ms.Myles and Sofia Fly that aims to provide a platform where Trans women (the Dolls), and Trans people have their voices and stories amplified. November 21st will be the biggest, boldest, and most impactful edition yet at Osler Records. November 20th is known internationally as Trans Day of Remembrance and is historically and politically the most significant of the days for the Trans community. It is a day to mourn and celebrate the lives of the trans people lost due to violence or suicide. It is a heavy day that carries a lot of emotional weight, which is something we seek to hold space for without compromising the goal of having a gathering and celebrating our trans present and giving hope to our trans futures by fundraising for recipients at GEORGE CHUVALO NEIGHBOURHOOD CENTRE & RAINBOW RAILROAD. item.title: Ojiichan's Dragon Toronto Book Launch — Sun Nov 22, 1:00 PM — Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
item.description: Join us at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre (JCCC) on Sunday, November 22nd, 2026 from 1:00pm - 3:00pm ET as we celebrate Jeff Chiba Stearns' newest graphic novel, Ojiichan's Dragon! Jeff Chiba Stearns is a fourth-generation Japanese Canadian illustrator and author who will share behind-the-scenes insights on the creative process and making of Ojiichan's Dragon. He is an Emmy nominated, multi-award-winning filmmaker, illustrator and author. His visual storytelling focuses on themes of history, cultural heritage, and family across animation, documentary, and books. Ojiichan's Dragon is Jeff's 3rd graphic novel. We will then be joined by Erica H. Isomura, illustrator of the non-fiction children's book Asahi: Japanese Canadian Baseball Heroes, and Dr. Lara Okihiro, co-author of children's novel, Obaasan's Boots, for a Japanese Canadian panel discussion and Q&A session. item.title: Collective Body — Wed Dec 9, 12:00 AM — Off Campus Koffler Arts
item.description:
Collective Body
About the Exhibition Presented as part of OCAD University’s 150th Anniversary Program, Collective Body is a multidisciplinary project by Gülay Alpay, selected and awarded for support through the anniversary program. Bringing together installation, performance, wearable art, photography, and experimental 16mm film, the exhibition explores inclusivity, connection, collective identity, and shared responsibility. Rooted in the belief that art can bring people together, Collective Body invites OCAD U students, faculty, alumni, and staff to participate in a shared creative experience that celebrates community, collaboration, and belonging. At the heart of the exhibition is a large-scale wearable dress that functions as both a sculptural installation and a living artwork. Activated through movement and collective participation, the dress becomes a symbol of unity, carrying individual memories, emotions, and experiences within a shared body.
